title: Rowan Bell · Community Manager · call with Rafe Ashbourne · February 2024

blocks.text: Call to check in on childcare co-op operations heading into the late winter sniffle season.

It’s been a week, Rowan. Good you called. The main thing is we finally got that backup network up. I organized it through Meadow Mutual Aid, so if a parent wakes up with a fever or their kid’s quarantined, they can send a quick message to the group. Another family who’s free that day can step in to cover their co-op shift or even take the extra child for a few hours. We’ve already used it twice this month—once when Milo’s dad got that stomach bug going around, and once when a neighbor’s mom had a last-minute shift change at the mill. It’s just a list of who’s available when, but it stopped two full-day closures.
That’s a huge relief for everyone. Anything else new on the ground?

Oh, the other small win. We had a parents’ meeting and everyone agreed the toy bin was becoming a petri dish. So I created a rotating schedule for toy sanitizing. It’s just a laminated checklist by the sink—wipe down, air dry, put back. Each family takes a week. It’s not glamorous, but it’s working. No more side-eyeing the sticky blocks. Keeps things clean and spreads the chore so no one feels overburdened.
Honestly, both things are just about making the system resilient. The backup plan for the people, the checklist for the stuff. It lets the parents breathe a little easier, and that’s the whole point.
